h1: Ozone Park Nan — hundreds-a-night, mid rice field in Pua, breathing the ozone below the Doi Phu Kha range
intro: Picture this: you wake up, open the bungalow door, and there's a sweep of green rice fields running all the way to the Doi Phu Kha range, cool air with the smell of earth and grass, birdsong instead of traffic — Ozone Park Nan is a small bungalow resort along the road beside the irrigation canal in Ban Nat, Pua District, and it plays on the name "ozone" for good reason: it really is quiet, open, and lets you live with nature, lungs full · this isn't a luxury resort but a few-hundred-baht stay for people who come to Pua for the rice fields, the mountain views and the calm, with just a handful of bungalow rooms — AC, fridge, view balcony — plus open grounds, a garden, picnic and BBQ corners, and free bikes to borrow · from about THB 750/night, around 3.6 km from Pua market.

body.html: Who Ozone Park Nan is for — the shortest way to put it: Ozone Park Nan is a stay for people who come to Pua and want "rice fields and mountains" to be the first thing they see in the morning, without paying thousands or tens of thousands a night · it's not a luxury resort with staff opening your car door, not a boutique hotel in the old town selling design, and not a streamside place packed with activities · it's a small bungalow resort along the road beside the irrigation canal in Ban Nat, Chai Watthana subdistrict, Pua District, whose main selling point is simplicity, quiet, and the nature all around · the name "ozone" captures the feel exactly: good air, open and easy, up close with the fields and the Doi Phu Kha ridgeline · the people it suits best are couples who want to escape the noise and stay somewhere quiet, small families road-tripping Nan who want a budget base, nature-minded travellers who don't mind the lack of luxury, and groups of friends who want to sit out and BBQ with a view in the evening · on the flip side, if you expect a big pool, a spa, a gym, or five-star hotel service, this isn't the answer — look at higher-tier stays in Nan town instead · to put it plainly, Ozone Park Nan sells the setting and the price, not luxury, and that's the expectation to set before you book.

Location and getting there — Ozone Park Nan is at 188 Moo 4, Liap Khlong Chonprathan Road, Ban Nat, Chai Watthana subdistrict, Pua District, Nan Province · the appeal of the location is that it sits a little outside Pua town, amid rice fields and farmland, so it's quieter and more open than places in the market area · the distances to know before you set off: it's about 3.6–3.7 km from Pua market, a few minutes' drive to find food or shop · and about 61–65 km from Nan Nakhon Airport (NNT), roughly one to one and a half hours by car, since Pua sits about 60 km north of Nan town · the thing to stress is that this place suits people with their own car or a rental most of all, because Pua is a district where the sights are spread out and public transport is limited · using Pua as a base, you can drive on up to Doi Phu Kha National Park, head to the Bo Kluea rock-salt wells, or stop at Wat Phuket and various viewpoints with ease · note that the roads around Pua heading up the mountain are winding and some stretches are unlit, so plan to travel in daylight and keep the tank full · if you fly into Nan without a car, arrange a transfer or charter a vehicle in advance, because finding a ride from the airport up to Pua without a booking can be more of a hassle than you'd think.

"Voices from real reviews of this kind of Pua stay tend to agree on the same thing: you wake up, open the door, and rice fields and mountains fill your eyes, the air is cool, it's quiet enough to hear birds — a setting worth the long drive, even if the rooms are simple."

Room types and decor — Ozone Park Nan is a small place of just a few bungalows; per the booking platforms there are only a handful of rooms, which keeps the feel friendly and uncrowded · the basic room is a twin with AC, a fridge, a flat-screen TV and an en-suite bathroom, and many bungalows have a balcony or front porch where you can sit and look out over the mountains and fields · the decor leans simple and clean in the style of budget upcountry stays — no luxe design work, but a warm garden-home feel · what to understand before booking is that, being a small, few-hundred-baht stay, the in-room amenities are basic rather than a spacious suite kitted out like a big hotel · if the view matters to you, ask at booking which rooms face the rice fields and mountains, because places like this usually have both bungalows with a full open view and ones where the view is partly blocked · another thing small Pua stays often get praised for is the cleanliness of the linens and bathrooms, which the owners tend to look after themselves and so pay attention to detail · overall, judged by the standard of a budget stay out in nature, the rooms at Ozone Park Nan are honestly good value: you pay a few hundred baht to sleep comfortably in a setting you can't get in town.

Facilities, activity grounds and common areas — small as it is, Ozone Park Nan positions itself as both a stay and an outdoor activity space · the highlight here is the open grounds, garden, picnic corner and BBQ (barbecue) zone, perfect for sitting in a circle with friends or family in the evening, breathing Pua's cool air with a view over the fields · there are free bikes to borrow for riding around to take in the rice fields and village life, an activity that fits the rural feel of Ban Nat very well · there's also open space and a garden-like setting that's sometimes used as a lawn for small parties and weddings, taking around a dozen-plus guests, with Thai buffet catering on offer · for basic services there's free parking (for about 15 cars), free Wi-Fi throughout, and a front desk on hand · some listings mention a balcony, a sitting terrace, and activities like cycling or fishing nearby · to be straight about it, Ozone Park Nan has no standard swimming pool, spa or gym like a big resort — the draw is the outdoor space and the atmosphere rather than luxe facilities · anyone picturing soaking in a pool with a view may need to adjust expectations, because the charm here is the open-air BBQ lawn and riding a bike around, more than anything else.

Food and on-site dining — Ozone Park Nan offers on-site dining; the booking platforms note à la carte breakfast and a restaurant or kitchen to support it · for parties and larger groups there's Thai buffet catering from about THB 250 per person, which shows the place is fairly geared toward small parties and events · what keeps food from being a big issue is the location: it's only about 3.6 km from Pua market, a few minutes' drive to the many local eateries, coffee shops and rice-field cafés Pua has on offer, like the well-known coffee-shop strip and the mid-field cafés that are this district's signature · so many people staying somewhere like this opt for a light breakfast at the property and then go café- and restaurant-hunting around Pua late morning and at lunch and dinner · in the evening, if you'd rather not go anywhere, picking up ingredients from Pua market to grill at the property's own BBQ lawn is a choice that fits the setting and saves money · overall, food isn't the reason to come to Ozone Park Nan for in-house dining, but a flexible extra that suits using the place as a base to explore Pua's food scene.

Service — for a small stay like Ozone Park Nan, service is tied directly to the owner and a small team · the strength of a place like this in Pua, which reviews tend to agree on, is friendliness and attentive care — the owners often give better tips on routes up Doi Phu Kha, viewpoints and local eateries than a big chain hotel would · there's a front desk to take requests and help coordinate parking, setting up the BBQ lawn, or events · that said, to be straight, understand that a small place at this level may not have staff on duty 24 hours like a big hotel, and English may be limited; if you arrive late or need urgent help, give notice in advance and get a direct contact number · overall the service here leans sincere rather than chain-hotel professional, which for anyone coming for an easy, relaxed stay fits the mood well.

Voices from real reviews (praise and gripes) — to be straight first: Ozone Park Nan is a small, newly opened place and still has few public reviews on the booking platforms; some platforms don't show an overall score yet · so the picture we've put together draws on the property's own information and on reviews of similar stays in Pua District that reflect the same trends, so you can set expectations right · on the praise side, what rice-field-view stays in Pua consistently get is the quiet setting and good air, the rice-field-and-mountain views that are lovely especially on misty mornings, the affordable price, the open grounds and BBQ corner that are nice to chill at, and friendly owners · on the watch-out side for this kind of place: the rooms and facilities are basic, not luxe; there may be insects or mosquitoes that come with rural land in the middle of fields; you need your own car to get around; and being a small stay, it may not have 24-hour service · most of these gripes come with choosing a budget stay out in nature rather than being faults of the property itself, and they're fixable with preparation and setting the right expectations.

"People who pick this kind of place in Pua tend to end up feeling the same way: you come for the setting and the view, not for luxury. If you can make peace with simple rooms and mosquitoes in the fields, the quiet and the view you get are worth the few hundred baht you pay."

Price comparison and value — Ozone Park Nan's starting rate is about THB 750/night for a twin room, which puts it among the most budget-friendly stays in Pua District · compared with boutique rice-field-view stays in Pua that usually start around THB 1,000–1,500/night and up, or resorts with a pool that climb higher still, Ozone Park Nan feels like value in the "pay the least to sleep in the middle of a rice field" sense · what you get is the setting, the quiet, mountain views, a BBQ lawn and free bikes, at less than half the price of a boutique stay · what you trade away is luxury, a pool, and full-service amenities · for a budget Nan road-trip where the room is just a place to sleep at night before heading out by day, this is a very sensible choice · but if your budget stretches to the low thousands and you want a pool or a nicer room, a boutique stay in Pua is worth comparing side by side before you decide.

Good to know before booking — a few things make a stay at Ozone Park Nan go more smoothly · one, bring your own car or rent one, since the property is outside Pua town and sights like Doi Phu Kha and Bo Kluea need a further drive · two, call or message the property directly to confirm availability and rates, because a small place like this can fill up fast at times and platform info may not always be up to date — the property has a Facebook channel (Ozone Park Nan), email and LINE to reach them · three, bring mosquito repellent and make peace with insects in the fields, since it's right by paddies and gardens · four, if you want to use the BBQ lawn or hold a party, give notice in advance so they can prepare the space and gear, and ask about bringing your own drinks · five, in Nan's high season (November–January), when the air is cool and the rice fields are green and lovely, Pua gets crowded and stays fill quickly, so book ahead · six, if you arrive after dark, ask for clear coordinates and landmarks, because parts of the canal-side road are dimly lit and hard to find in the dark.

The verdict — Ozone Park Nan is the best fit for people who want to stay in the middle of Pua's rice fields for a few hundred baht, with a quiet setting and views of the Doi Phu Kha range · the picnic-BBQ lawn, free bikes, free parking and a location just a few kilometres from Pua market make it a budget, easygoing base for exploring Pua, in a straightforward way · if you're after luxury, a pool, a spa, or big-hotel service, this isn't the answer, and you should consider a boutique stay in Pua or a hotel in Nan town instead · but for a Nan road trip where you want a good-value stay, life with nature with your lungs full, waking up to rice fields and mountains, and a BBQ corner to chill at with friends in the evening — Ozone Park Nan answers that need on the lightest budget · since it's a small stay with still few public reviews, we'd recommend contacting the property directly to confirm the details before every trip, to make your Pua trip as smooth as possible.
